prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: tileable diffuse albedo material for an actual 3D shallow tropical marine reef limestone substrate, not a finished underwater scene. Primary request: a square straight-on flat orthographic material swatch showing naturally colonised old carbonate reef pavement, with broad irregular connected areas of muted olive-brown and warm grey encrusting biofilm, restrained dusty rose coralline patches, and a smaller amount of exposed weathered cream limestone. Medium scale connected blotches should carry the overall colour; fine texture should be subtle, softly resolved and low contrast so it does not become salt-and-pepper noise from several metres away. Aged marine carbonate, gentle pits and erosion, documentary natural material quality. Uniform flat diffuse illumination: absolutely no cast shadows, directional highlights, lens effects or water tint. No distinct coral colonies, fish, plants, moss, terrestrial granite, pebbles, dramatic cracks, symbols, text or watermark. No white-dominant surface, no saturated colours. Opposite edges should visually match; no central hero feature. This is an authored colour texture, not a measured photogrammetric scan. Opaque full-frame texture.

references.use: Calcium carbonate reef foundation; not the source of measured material colour or a photograph.
Distinction between colonial coral animals, skeletal reef structure and habitat; no image copied.

use: Sample-only substrate diffuse colour. Generated source copied unchanged into the project; broad subdued colour areas replace the white-dominant prior texture. Same file and 0.24 per-metre triplanar scale used in WebGL material and native albedo preview.
limits: Authored palette and requested tile continuity, not a surveyed substrate, measured biological cover, taxonomic identification or calibrated PBR. No generated normal or roughness map. Offline appearance does not establish WebGL lighting or documentary realism.
